title: Role-play lab: six “wrong time” conversations
objectives: Answer six “wrong time” conversations with diagnosis, not prediction.
Use the module's scenario answers (Q21–Q25) as trainer-marked practice.
body_md:
In pairs. One person plays the client, the other explains — in plain words, with a rupee example.

| Client says | Explain |
| --- | --- |
| “I invested ₹10 lakh last year and it's down 12%. I picked the wrong time. Should I exit?” | Diagnose the cause and discuss the horizon. |
| “The market fell 15%. Should I stop my SIP until it settles?” | Explain why SIPs work through falls. |
| “I have ₹25 lakh from a property sale. I'll wait for a crash before investing.” | Discuss the cost of waiting and offer an STP. |
| “My fund is down but so is everything. Should I switch funds?” | Compare with the benchmark and category. |
| A retiree's portfolio fell 20% just after retirement. | Discuss sequence risk, the income buffer and the SWP amount. |
| “I just want my money back, then I'll get out.” | Address loss aversion and anchoring. |

> **Investor takeaway:** Quiz scenarios Q21–Q25 (trainer-marked): a scenario answer earns its mark if it covers at least three model points and makes no promise of returns.
example: Role-play the peak investor: acknowledge first, then horizon, benchmark, keep SIPs going, add gradually if comfortable.
say: Acknowledge the client's frustration before explaining.
never: Predict when the market will recover.
Dismiss the client's concern as irrational.

check.q: Mr. Rao invested ₹10 L as a lump sum in January 2020 and is down sharply in March. He wants to exit. His goal is 10 years away. What do you do?
o: Advise exiting to stop the loss

Acknowledge the frustration; confirm the 10-year horizon; compare the fund with its benchmark; explain the fall is market-wide; keep SIPs going and, if comfortable, add gradually; share history with “no guarantee”; record the discussion
check.why: Acknowledge the frustration; confirm the 10-year horizon; compare the fund with its benchmark from the same date; explain that the fall is market-wide; keep his SIPs going and, if comfortable, add gradually. Share history with “no guarantee”. Record the discussion.

check.q: Ms. Shah has ₹25 L from a property sale and says she’ll invest “after the next crash”. What do you offer?
o: Agree to wait for the crash

Show the cost of waiting with an illustrative example; offer an STP from a liquid fund over 6–12 months to reduce regret, or agree written trigger rules; don’t predict a crash or promise better timing
Invest it all in small caps now
check.why: Show the cost of waiting with an illustrative example; offer an STP from a liquid fund over 6–12 months to reduce regret; or agree written trigger rules. Don’t predict a crash or promise better timing.

check.q: A client put her daughter’s wedding money (needed in 14 months) into a mid-cap fund, which has now fallen 15%. What is the plan?
o: Wait for it to recover, however long it takes
Diagnose: wrong category for a short horizon. Plan a move towards debt or liquid funds on a schedule, considering tax and exit loads, rather than panic-selling in one go; document the reasoning
Add more to the mid-cap fund
check.why: Diagnose: wrong category for a short horizon. Plan a move towards debt or liquid funds on a schedule, considering tax and exit loads, rather than panic-selling in one go. Document the reasoning.
